sourceDirectedNegativeEdges.actualIndividualCoreContrastAndBoundary: Matter/event versus thing/object is an introductory core contrast, NOT universal abstract/concrete separation. Both the whole 物 lesson and the separately attested 事（じ）phenomenon sense prevent an all-senses claim.
Matter/event versus speaking/conversation are the displayed cores. 話 can concern a matter or an account of an event; this does not establish universal disjointness.
Matter/event versus strength/power. Work or an affair can involve power, but that shared situation does not equate these displayed lexical cores.
Leaving/elapsing versus earth/soil. The visible 土 in the mnemonic is not the whole meaning of 去 or proof of historical composition.
Leaving/elapsing versus support/platform or the bound equipment counter. A bound counting use is not a standalone departure meaning.
Leaving/elapsing versus public/official. Shared readings or contexts do not equate the displayed cores; no universal sense inventory is claimed.
Selling versus buying identifies opposite participant roles in one transaction. Their shared transaction domain is retained, not treated as absolute semantic separation.
Selling versus reading. Similar modern right-hand shapes do not make 売 the meaning of 読 or establish a new historical derivation.
Selling versus earlier/ahead in time. Sale timing may involve precedence, but the stated core actions are different.
Returning home versus writing. Do not turn visual comparison or co-occurrence in a text into lexical equivalence.
Returning home versus building. A home can be built or returned to; the common home setting is not the same predicate.
Returning home versus use/purpose. Rare dictionary readings おくる/とつぐ remain available within their attested character senses; they do not prove universal disjointness or ordinary frequency.
Building versus passage/attendance. Building a passage is a shared situation, not lexical identity; 廴 and 辶 are different modern outlines.
Building versus writing. Written plans or 建て financial uses do not establish that the displayed construction core means writing.
Building versus matter/event. A construction project can be an affair, but the action and the broad event noun are not identical displayed cores.
Stopping/ceasing versus correctness. The extra top horizontal distinguishes the modern shapes; it is not evidence that correctness means stopping.
Stopping/ceasing versus upward/above. Something may stop above a point; that context is not core lexical equivalence.
Stopping/ceasing versus exiting/appearing. Ending an activity may involve leaving; retain that domain boundary rather than declaring every やめる and 出る sense disjoint.
Correctness versus stopping/ceasing, separately judged in this source direction. A modern shape relation does not equate the meanings or automatically justify a reverse quiz verdict.
Correctness versus five. Shape comparison is a recognition aid, not a meaning or etymology rule.
Correctness versus earth/soil. The shared horizontal and vertical strokes do not equate their displayed meanings.
Walking/steps versus stopping/ceasing. The mnemonic's visible 止 is not the whole meaning of 歩; no historical foot-origin claim is inferred from this contrast.
Walking versus running are different modes of movement. Both have figurative extensions, and 走る also describes vehicles; NOT universal movement-domain separation.
Walking/steps versus few/a little. Comparison of lower strokes is visual only, not a claim that 少 supplies the whole meaning of 歩.
Departure/emission versus meeting. A meeting can begin, but the common event setting does not equate these displayed cores.
Departure/emission versus selling. Product release can precede or accompany sale; retain that connection, not a claim that all release/sale uses are unrelated.
Departure/emission versus older brother. Similar lower legs do not equate their meanings or establish historical composition.
Running versus rising/arising. Both can concern movement or starting activity; the different represented cores do not establish all-sense disjointness.
Running versus foot/leg. The body part and the action are related, not identical; vehicles also 走る without human feet.
Running versus red. This is the stated action/color core contrast, not an etymological explanation of either shape.
Rising/arising versus running, separately considered in this direction. 起つ is attested for rising to action, not an automatic substitute for every ordinary 立つ.
Rising/arising versus foot/leg. A body part can participate in getting up, but is not the predicate.
Rising/arising versus color. This represented core contrast does not deny other attested senses of either character.
Nearness versus sending/escorting. Shared 辶 or a nearby destination does not make the displayed meanings equivalent.
Nearness versus road/way. A road may be short or nearby; that does not make proximity and a route the same core meaning.
Nearness versus week. Temporal nearness can describe a week, but 週 itself denotes the seven-day unit.
Sending/escorting versus nearness, separately judged in this direction. The destination's distance does not define the sending action.
Sending/escorting versus passage/attendance. Communication and transportation domains overlap; the proposed contrast is between displayed cores, not universal lexical separation.
Sending/escorting versus week. A recurring delivery can be weekly; scheduling is not lexical identity.
Passage/attendance versus sending/escorting, separately judged. Transmission/communication senses can overlap, so not an all-senses or ordinary-fallback-safety verdict.
Passage/attendance versus week. Repeated attendance can follow a weekly schedule, but the action and the time unit remain different represented cores.
Passage/attendance versus nearness. A route may pass nearby; common 辶 and spatial context do not equate the cores.
Week versus carrying/luck. Periodic transportation is a shared situation, not the same lexical core.
Week versus passage/attendance, separately judged. A regular attendance schedule does not turn 通 into the seven-day unit.
Week versus road/way. The mnemonic's seven-day route is not an etymology or an assertion that 週 means road.
Carrying/luck versus week. A weekly transport schedule does not equate either movement or fortune with the time unit.
Carrying/luck versus passage/attendance. Movement/transport domains overlap; the carrying and attendance cores are distinct without all-senses disjointness.
Carrying/luck versus reaching/plural suffix. Delivery and reaching a destination overlap in the wider domain; retain this limitation, not universal separation.
Reaching/plural suffix versus friend. In 友達, the whole friend word is not the standalone meaning of its suffix; the lexicalized whole may denote one or several friends.
Reaching/plural suffix versus meeting. Groups may meet and goals may be attained at meetings; these contexts do not equate the displayed cores.
Reaching/plural suffix versus going/travelling. Attaining a destination and travelling are related; 達 also has attested passage senses. This is not universal separation or frequency approval.
